original_question: For the coefficients x^pi_m(lambda, kappa) defined by expanding the osp(1|2) polynomials P_pi(lambda, kappa) in powers of c0 + d0^2 and d0^2, is every coefficient x^pi_m(lambda, kappa) always an integer for all allowed lambda, kappa, pi, and m?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1 in Section 8: the integrality of the expansion coefficients x_m^π(λ,κ) of the osp(1|2) polynomials P^π(λ,κ); the precise expansion is restated in Appendix B, eqs. (B.3)-(B.6).
correct_elements: Your draft is aimed at the right paper target: the paper's Conjecture 1 about the coefficients x appearing when the Section 8 osp(1|2) polynomials P^π(λ,κ) are expanded in the variables c0 + d0^2 and d0^2. You also correctly treat the question as an integrality question for all admissible indices, rather than as a request for an explicit formula.
missing_details: The paper does not use a bare expansion of P^π(λ,κ); it first factors off (d0)^τ_π, where τ_ρ := [ρ + 1/2] - [ρ] is the parity indicator of a spin ρ.
The precise expansion is P^π(λ,κ) = (d0)^τ_π sum_{m=0}^{[π]} x_m^π(λ,κ) (c0 + d0^2)^[π]-m (d0^2)^m, so the range of m is exactly 0 <= m <= [π].
The paper explicitly states that π (written also as ω in Appendix B) may be integral or half-integral; [π] denotes its integral part.
A stand-alone formulation should say that P^π(λ,κ)/(d0)^τ_π is homogeneous of degree [π] in the pair of variables (c0 + d0^2, d0^2).
The coefficients x_m^π(λ,κ) depend on admissible osp(1|2) spin labels λ and κ; these are nonnegative integral or half-integral ranks occurring in the closure relation that defines P^π(λ,κ).
The conjecture is about integer values of x_m^π(λ,κ) at admissible spin labels, not about formal integrality of coefficients in an abstract polynomial ring in λ and κ.
For π > 1, the paper notes the extra restriction x_[π]^π(λ,κ) = 0, equivalently that c0 + d0^2 factors from P^π(λ,κ); this is part of the nearby context even though it is not the conjecture itself.

The ambient variables c0 and d0 come from the two-parameter tensor-operator construction S^κ(c0,d0); the draft does not currently say that the conjecture is tied to that specific osp(1|2) closure-relation setting.
No nilpotency hypothesis is part of this conjecture, and there is no phrase like 'for all sufficiently large m' here; the quantifier on m is finite and explicit.
refined_question:
Let τ_ρ := [ρ + 1/2] - [ρ], so τ_ρ = 0 for integral ρ and τ_ρ = 1 for half-integral ρ. For the osp(1|2) closure-relation polynomials P^π(λ,κ) introduced in Section 8 (with admissible spin labels λ, κ, π in 1/2 N_0), write
P^π(λ,κ) = (d0)^τ_π sum_{m=0}^{[π]} x_m^π(λ,κ) (c0 + d0^2)^[π]-m (d0^2)^m,
so that P^π(λ,κ)/(d0)^τ_π is homogeneous of degree [π] in c0 + d0^2 and d0^2 (and, for π > 1, x_[π]^π(λ,κ)=0). Is Conjecture 1 true: for every admissible λ, κ, π and every m = 0,1,...,[π], is x_m^π(λ,κ) always an integer?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper's actual open problem. The introduction explicitly says that Section 8 produces closure relations involving polynomials P^π(λ,κ), that these polynomials are expanded using coefficients x over powers of d0^2 and c0 + d0^2, and that 'coefficients x are integers (conjecture 1)'. Appendix B then gives the precise general expansion, the degree/homogeneity statement, and the range of m, while Section 6.1 defines the parity factor τ_ρ that must be included in the formula. So the paper-faithful sharpened question is exactly the integer-valuedness of the coefficients x_m^π(λ,κ) in that specific expansion, not a broader question about arbitrary osp(1|2) polynomial coefficients.
